title: Kansas August 2026 ex parte renewal share
question: What percentage of Kansas Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries due for renewal in August 2026 will have coverage renewed on an ex parte basis in CMS's first published original (O) submission?
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Kansas's ex parte renewal share for the August 2026 reporting period, computed from the original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it. Compute 100 times Beneficiaries Whose Coverage Was Renewed on an Ex Parte Basis divided by Beneficiaries with a Renewal Due, using both counts as first published, and round to one decimal. Later corrections and updated (U) submissions do not affect resolution.
drivers: Recent Kansas original-submission shares near 47 percent
Modest allowance for the prior summer's cohort pattern
Eligibility data matching and renewal-form classification
Two unobserved reporting months after the latest available period

reasoning.text: Kansas August 2026 original-submission ex parte renewal share

The target is the Kansas state row for reporting_period=202608 and original_or_updated=O in dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c. CMS's state outcome table defines the denominator as all beneficiaries due for renewal, including pending cases: Metric 5a1 divided by Metric 5. The forecast concerns the original, preliminary monthly outcome, with no seasonal adjustment. Every historical anchor uses the same O variant as currently exposed by CMS; historical first-publication snapshots were not separately reconstructed.

reasoning.call: Fetched the CMS datastore API for Kansas original submissions during January–December 2025; read counts from the echoed JSON response.
reasoning.result: Relevant fetched ex parte/due counts: June 2025 14690/38257; July 11442/31779; August 15946/36356; September 16017/32956; October 18880/34051; November 22218/39631; December 16277/30480. Calculated shares are respectively 38.398202, 36.004909, 43.860711, 48.601165, 55.446242, 56.062174 and 53.402231 percent.

reasoning.call: Fetched the CMS datastore API for Kansas original submissions with reporting_period>=202601; read counts from the echoed JSON response.
reasoning.result: The response contains six rows, January–June 2026. Fetched ex parte/due counts: January 15260/33796; February 11883/25992; March 15421/30165; April 16944/36241; May 17999/38980; June 19188/40362. Calculated shares are respectively 45.153273, 45.717913, 51.122161, 46.753677, 46.174962 and 47.539765 percent.

reasoning.text: The outside-view reference class is 13 consecutive Kansas O monthly observations from June 2025 through June 2026. Their unweighted base rate is 47.2490 percent; the latest six-month mean is 47.0770 percent. These comparable state observations anchor the forecast before any summer adjustment.

reasoning.call: Opened the official June 2026 CMS snapshot and located the Kansas row in Coverage Retention and Disenrollment Rates by State, printed page 30.
reasoning.result: The Kansas row reports 40362 beneficiaries due, 82 percent renewed, 15 percent disenrolled, 3 percent pending and 48 percent renewed ex parte. Its whole-percent ex parte statistic agrees with 100*19188/40362=47.539765 percent from the original-submission API row. Source: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/downloads/eligib-oper-and-enrol-snap-jun2026.pdf.

reasoning.text: Calendar verification limitation: the official CMS announcement archive lists June 2026 released September 25, 2026, but exposes no scheduled August 2026 publication date. December 15, 2026 is retained solely as the contractual resolutionDate; it could not be verified from an official release calendar or announcement this run. The mandatory date-verification requirement therefore remains unmet. Source: https://www.medicaid.gov/medicaid-and-chip-eligibility-operations-and-enrollment-snapshot.

Level: use June's 47.5398 percent persistence anchor, close to both reference-class means. Momentum: add zero because recent changes alternate in sign. Cohort effect: the June-to-August 2025 increase was 5.4625 percentage points; apply an analyst-selected 25 percent weight because a single prior summer provides weak seasonal evidence. One-off and policy-mechanism adjustments: add zero without verified evidence of a new Kansas implementation. CMS explains that automation completed after a form is sent can be classified as form-based renewal, making reported ex parte shares sensitive to workflow.

Prior/update/interval: Persistence prior with a weak summer-cohort adjustment; historical sample is 13 unrounded Kansas O shares, June 2025–June 2026. Point = 47.539765 + 0.25*(43.860711-38.398202) + 0 momentum + 0 one-off + 0 policy = 48.905392, rounded to 48.9 percent. The 12 successive changes are -2.3933, 7.8558, 4.7405, 6.8451, 0.6159, -2.6599, -8.2490, 0.5646, 5.4042, -4.3685, -0.5787 and 1.3648 percentage points; their mean is 0.761797. Sample sigma = 4.825222 percentage points, computed as sqrt(sum((change-0.761797)^2)/11). The approximate Gaussian 80 percent one-month half-width is 1.28*sigma = 6.176284 points. For the two-month June-to-August horizon, assuming independent monthly innovations, multiply by sqrt(2): half-width = 8.734584. Unrounded bounds are 40.170808 and 57.639977 percent; final bounds are 40.2 and 57.6 percent.

Upside risk: an August cohort with more readily verified income records or improved automatic matching raises ex parte renewals. Downside risk: matching failures, more complex cases or renewals classified as form-based reduce the share. A substantial automation improvement could land above 57.6 percent, outside the interval; a disrupted renewal batch or markedly less matchable cohort could land below 40.2 percent, outside the interval. The single prior summer may reflect transitional processing rather than repeatable seasonality.
